capitals.name: Stanleyville (Kisangani)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Stanleyville'; coordinates are the gazetteer's for Kisangani.

rulers.name: Antoine Gizenga
rulers.title: Head of the Stanleyville government
rulers.note: Declared the government on 12 December 1960; First Deputy Prime Minister in Adoula's coalition from 2 August 1961, then back in Stanleyville from September 1961; censured on 15 January 1962 and flown to Léopoldville on 20 January 1962.

correction.text: Orientale Province, the base of the Free Republic; the ledger adds Bukavu (24 December 1960), northern Kivu and a strip of northern Katanga (by 10 January 1961), Sankuru and Maniema (October 1961)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The page gives no area or population; Orientale resolves to about 467,865 km2 in the gazetteer. Whole-province control is the page's 'Gizenga's military strength in Orientale Province rapidly increased', not a survey.

ledger.note: 1960: Antoine Gizenga declares the Free Republic of the Congo at Stanleyville. 'On 12 December 1960, Gizenga declared his new government, the Free Republic of the Congo,' 'based in Orientale Province, the legitimate ruling authority in the Congo.' The Congo Crisis page says the rebel government formed 'in November 1960'.

24 December 1960: 'Stanleyville troops occupied Bukavu and arrested the local army commander.' On 1 January 1961 central troops advised by Belgians entered from Ruanda and occupied the Saio camp but were pushed back into Ruanda. The 50 km radius is a reading.

January 1961: 'Gizenga's authority was also established over the Sankuru District of Kasai Province.' The page places the sentence between 'By 10 January, Stanleyville forces had occupied northern Katanga as far in as Manono' and 'Around then, control had been consolidated in Goma and the northern Kivu region', so the month is January 1961 (reviewer af-08-f, 2026-10-19; previously undated at confidence 1). The Lodja radius is a reading of the district.

region.text: Goma and the northern Kivu region

ledger.note: By 10 January 1961 'control had been consolidated in Goma and the northern Kivu region.' Fire was exchanged across the Ruanda border at Goma-Gisenyi on 12 January 1961 over fears of a Belgian-backed invasion.

region.text: northern Katanga as far in as Manono

ledger.note: By 10 January 1961 'Stanleyville forces had occupied northern Katanga as far in as Manono' without resistance. The page does not say the State of Katanga held the strip; it is the province Katanga claimed. The 150 km radius round Manono is a reading.
October 1961: 'Pro-Gizenga administrators were installed in the Maniema and Sankuru districts.' The Kindu atrocity of 11 November 1961 (13 Italian UN aviators murdered) is not a capture.

region.text: Orientale, Bukavu, northern Kivu, Sankuru and Maniema

ledger.note: January 1962: Gizenga is censured by Parliament on 15 January and flown to Léopoldville on 20 January; the infobox gives 'Disestablished: 16 January 1962'. 'The rival government was not fully reintegrated into the Republic of the Congo until Gizenga was arrested in January 1962.'

region.text: the Manono strip of northern Katanga

ledger.note: January 1962: the page is silent on what became of the northern Katanga strip when the Stanleyville regime ended; it falls back to the Katanga claim until January 1963. Placed at confidence 1.

region.text: the lands of the Stanleyville regime

ledger.note: January 1962: the Free Republic ends with Gizenga's arrest; its land passes to the Republic of the Congo (identity.successors).

wars.name: Congo Crisis (Stanleyville government)
wars.outcome: The regime ended politically, not by conquest, in January 1962: Gizenga joined Adoula's coalition on 2 August 1961, returned to Stanleyville in September, was stripped of the vice premiership on 15 January 1962 and imprisoned at Camp Kokolo on 25 January.
wars.note: By 20 February 1961 sixteen states, among them the Soviet Union, China, Ghana, Guinea and Morocco, recognised the Free Republic as the legitimate government. Infobox status 'Partially recognized rival government'.

certainty.note: Control was by garrisons and administrators, not a frontier: the page gives provinces and districts (Orientale, northern Kivu, Sankuru, Maniema) and 'as far in as Manono', with no map.

sources.title: Free Republic of the Congo
sources.note: Established 12 December 1960 at Stanleyville, Bukavu 24 December 1960, northern Katanga to Manono and Goma by 10 January 1961, recognition 20 February 1961, Maniema and Sankuru October 1961, disestablished 16 January 1962.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks, written as a rebel dossier (held land for 13 months); the DRC dossier carries the matching losses (December 1960 to October 1961) and the gain back (January 1962), replacing the contest placeholder of the first draft. One page opened. Discrepancies: the Congo Crisis page says the rebel government formed 'in November 1960'; the Free Republic page declares it on 12 December 1960 (used). Regions are provinces and radii; the page has no map and no area, so the extent of real control beyond Orientale is a reading. The Sankuru gain is undated on the page (confidence 1). The northern Katanga strip is placed against the State of Katanga, whose dossier has the matching loss (January 1961) and gain back (January 1962, confidence 1). The reintegration of August 1961 (Gizenga as First Deputy Prime Minister) did not return the land and is a note, not an event. The People's Republic of the Congo of 1964 (Simba rebels, Stanleyville again) lasted months and has no dossier; see the DRC dossier's July-November 1964 contest. Family 'africa' is a placeholder for the colour agent.
